user.description: User account under which QEMU processes run. Use 'qemu' or a dedicated non-root user for security.

vnc_tls.description: Enable TLS encryption for VNC remote desktop connections. Required for secure access.

vnc_listen.description: IP address on which VNC servers listen. '127.0.0.1' restricts to local host; '0.0.0.0' allows all interfaces.

spice_listen.description: IP address on which SPICE servers listen. Similar to VNC, restrict to '127.0.0.1' for security.

spice_tls.description: Enable TLS encryption for SPICE remote desktop connections.

io_threads.description: Number of dedicated I/O worker threads. Higher values may improve I/O throughput on multi-core systems.

migration.description: Enable or disable VM live migration capability.

migration_address.description: IP address for incoming migration traffic. Use '0.0.0.0' to listen on all interfaces.

migration_port.description: Base port for migration traffic. Migrating VMs use sequential ports in the range.

migration_ports.description: Number of ports (starting from migration_port) reserved for concurrent migrations.

auto_memory_tune.description: Enable automatic memory tuning (e.g., hugepages, NUMA placement). Disable for manual control.

memory_backing.description: Memory backing mode for VMs. 'hugepages' improves performance on large guests.

image_paths.description: Search paths for VM disk images. Add custom paths as needed.

emulator.description: Override the default QEMU emulator binary (e.g., 'qemu-system-aarch64'). Leave empty to auto-detect.

sandbox.description: Enable seccomp sandboxing to restrict system calls. Keep enabled for security.

use_cgroups.description: Use cgroups v2 for CPU and memory resource control. Required for advanced QoS.

max_vcpus.description: Maximum virtual CPUs allowed per guest. Adjust based on host CPU topology.

default_cpu_model.description: Default CPU model exposed to guests. 'host-passthrough' exposes host features for best performance.

hotplug.description: Enable hotplug for disks and NICs. Required for dynamic resource scaling.

monitor_stdin.description: Enable QEMU monitor on stdin. Disable to prevent accidental console access.

monitor_protocol.description: Protocol used for QEMU monitor communication. 'json' is recommended for automation.

default_video_model.description: Default graphics adapter for VMs. 'qxl' works well with SPICE; 'virtio' for minimal overhead.

numa_auto_allocation.description: Automatically allocate guest memory to NUMA nodes. Disable for manual NUMA pinning.

uefi_firmware.description: Enable UEFI firmware support (OVMF/AAVMF). Required for UEFI guests.

uefi_firmware_paths.description: Paths to UEFI firmware binaries. Order matters if multiple architectures supported.

netns.description: Run QEMU processes in a private network namespace. Isolates network stack for security.

default_dns.description: DNS server used by guest VMs when using user-mode networking.

auto_bridge.description: Automatically create a bridge interface (e.g., virbr0) for NAT networking.

auto_bridge_name.description: Name of the auto-created bridge interface.

seccomp_sandbox.description: Enable seccomp filters to restrict system calls. Keep enabled unless troubleshooting.

vhost_user.description: Enable vhost-user (userspace virtio backend) support for high-performance networking.

tee.description: Enable support for Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) devices (e.g., Intel TDX).

tpm.description: Enable TPM (Trusted Platform Module) support in guests.

default_tpm_backend.description: Default TPM backend: 'emulator' uses software TPM, 'passthrough' uses host hardware TPM.

live_snapshot.description: Enable taking snapshots of running VMs without downtime.

shared_block.description: Allow multiple VMs to share the same block device. Requires external coordination (e.g., GFS2).

log_level.description: Logging verbosity: 0=none, 1=error, 2=info, 3=debug. Use 2 for general troubleshooting.

log_output.description: Where to send QEMU logs: 'file', 'syslog', or 'stderr'.

log_file.description: Path to the log file when log_output is set to 'file'.
